newsitem.title: USA: Midwest Cash Grain PM - No bids for rail corn.
newsitem.headline: Midwest Cash Grain PM - No bids for rail corn.

text.p: Dealers in rail corn markets said there were no bids on Thursday as end-users in the southeast turn to local corn to meet feed needs, dealers said.
"They're harvesting in Georgia and starting to harvest in South Carolina," said a rail broker.
As of Sunday, the USDA reported that as of Sunday, 21 percent of Georgia's and South Carolina's corn crop was mature.
Elsewhere, farmers in the eastern Corn Belt were waiting for fields to dry so they could resume wheat harvest as quickly as possible.
Although the bulk of the soft red winter wheat crop has been harvested, the week's rains have raised concerns that test weights for the wheat left in the fields will be lower than average.
"We'll probably see some degradation," said an Ohio dealer. "The rain washes some of the nutrients out of the head and lowers test weights."
Merchandisers reported only modest sales of grain and soybeans on Thursday.
